ratings_why.fun: Choosing where news starts and who stands where is a good puzzle, but working out halving per step at a glance is a chore without strong UI help.
ratings_why.distinct: Gains that spread and fade along a chain, a Taster turning other tribes' growth into news, and hits shared across the Huddle feel unlike today's tribes, though touching-run growth echoes Hedgerow.

verdict_why: The Knot keyword still doesn't say whether a tie pulls in one unit or that unit's whole run, which Hoarfrost Knotter and the Tied Council build depend on.

points.text: Knot says a tie makes a tied unit join, but not whether the units touching that unit join too, and 'first and last units' clashes with 'ties never change the ends'. Say plainly: a tie adds only the tied unit, and the ends are the ends of the zigzag run.

The Winter Huddle is the longest text in the tribe and can't be read at a glance. Put the rules in a keyword (say Huddle: hits on this are shared with its Knot neighbours) and keep the card to one line.
Print each Gossip's reach on the card or show it on hover (+2 reaches 1, +4 reaches 2), so Little Fips and the Town-Hall Crier read as spreading rather than as self-buffs.

We, the Rattenkönig removes the halving, so the position puzzle disappears at the top. A version that halves every two steps would keep position mattering while still feeling like the whole knot speaks as one.

standouts.why: Taster Wendelin tastes a neighbour's gain and passes it on as news: the real rat behaviour in one readable line.
Old Gundel making everyone gossip at once is the tickling scene from the seed, and the text is short.
Ilse repeating the biggest news is the minute-taker reading back the minutes; clear trigger, clear timing.

weakest.why: A strong idea buried under a paragraph of rules a player won't read mid-recruit.
Ratskeller Landlady is a plain gold trigger; the pub flavour doesn't show in what it does.
Cold-Shed Litter is a generic summon-a-token unit; only the Stray's role in the Knot ties it to the tribe.

flags.note: What a tie adds to the Knot (one unit or its whole run) and which units become the ends isn't settled by the keyword text.
Next to an Ooze that eats a big unit, Wendelin makes one huge piece of news, which Ilse can then repeat.
Speaker with the Mill-Chimney and the Rattenkönig gives every unit the full stats of a huge unit in a fight.
